title: Small Enough to Stick
outcomeStatement: By the end of this, you'll have one habit running that's too small to fail.

practices.title: Who is this for?
practices.body: One sentence: the kind of person you're trying to become. Not a goal — an identity. "Someone who moves every day" rather than "lose 8kg". Keep it. You'll come back to it on day 14.

practices.title: Score your day
practices.body: List everything you do in a normal day, in order, from waking to sleeping. Next to each, write + if it serves who you want to become, – if it works against it, = if it's neutral. No changes yet. Just look.

practices.title: Which of your current habits is voting for someone you don't want to be?
practices.body: Look at your minus column from yesterday before you start.

practices.title: Time and place, in writing
practices.body: Pick the one habit you most want. Write it as a single sentence: "I will [behaviour] at [time] in [place]." Vague intentions lose to specific ones every time. Put it somewhere you'll see it.

practices.cue: After something you already do every day without fail
practices.behavior: the two-minute version of your new habit
practices.title: Stack it onto something that already works
practices.body: Attach the new habit to an existing one so the existing habit becomes the reminder. Choose the two-minute version — not the ambitious one. Set the cue and behaviour now.

practices.title: Move one object
practices.body: Change one physical thing in one room so the habit is easier to start — the shoes by the door, the book on the pillow, the guitar out of its case. Environment beats motivation because it's still there tomorrow.

practices.title: What do you actually want out of the habit you keep failing at?
practices.body: Underneath the habit is usually something you want to feel or be. Find that.

practices.title: Pair it with something you want
practices.body: Take something you need to do and bind it to something you enjoy — the podcast you only allow yourself while walking, the coffee you only drink while writing. Write the pairing down and set it up today.

practices.title: One decision away
practices.body: Today, notice every moment where you were one small decision from the habit and didn't take it. Don't judge the moment. Just count how often the door was open.
practices.noticeFor: moments you were one decision from doing it

practices.title: Shrink it until it's laughable
practices.body: Take the habit you find hardest and cut it down to a version that takes under two minutes. "Read a chapter" becomes "read one page." Write the shrunken version. The point is starting, not achieving.

practices.title: Add friction to one thing
practices.body: Pick a habit you want less of. Add steps between you and it — log out, move the app off the home screen, unplug the thing, put it in another room. Make it take twenty seconds longer to start.

practices.behavior: leave the phone charging in another room
practices.title: The phone sleeps elsewhere
practices.body: The strongest version of making a habit harder is making it physically distant. Adjust the specifics to your setup if you need to.

practices.title: The simplest possible tracker
practices.body: Set up the least effortful way to mark the habit done — a wall calendar, a note, a line in a book. If tracking takes longer than the habit, it will not survive.

practices.title: Fourteen days ago you wrote who you were becoming. What's actually changed?
practices.body: Read day 1 first. Be honest about what moved and what didn't — the unmoved parts are the more useful information.
